claims.text: A build-plate temperature of approximately 400–500 °C is an appropriate elevated-preheat range for LPBF of AlCrFeNiSi.
Elevated build-plate preheating reduces the temperature differential between the melt pool and substrate and lessens solidification thermal gradients.
Elevated preheating lowers the melt-pool cooling rate.
Reduced thermal gradients encourage more uniform nucleation and equiaxed grain growth.
Slower, more uniform solidification suppresses rapid-solidification effects that cause compositional segregation.
Lower cooling rates and more uniform solidification reduce residual stress.
Slower, more uniform solidification produces a more homogeneous distribution of alloying elements.
Preheating is a commonly used approach to attenuate cracking in additively manufactured alloys.
Excessively high preheat temperatures can cause grain coarsening.
Controlling preheat within 400–500 °C should mitigate grain coarsening and remain within AlCrFeNiSi phase-stability limits.
Relative to room-temperature-build-plate LPBF, preheated AlCrFeNiSi will have a statistically significant reduction in residual stress.
Relative to room-temperature-build-plate LPBF, preheated AlCrFeNiSi will contain fewer microstructural defects.
Preheated AlCrFeNiSi will show less elemental segregation by EDX than room-temperature-build-plate LPBF material.
Preheated AlCrFeNiSi will have greater fracture toughness than room-temperature-build-plate LPBF material.
Preheated AlCrFeNiSi will have greater ductility than room-temperature-build-plate LPBF material.
Room-temperature-build-plate LPBF of AlCrFeNiSi typically produces high thermal gradients.
Room-temperature-build-plate LPBF of AlCrFeNiSi typically produces significant residual stresses.
Room-temperature-build-plate LPBF of AlCrFeNiSi typically produces pronounced elemental segregation.
Room-temperature-build-plate LPBF of AlCrFeNiSi typically produces a higher density of microcracks and porosity.
The proposed effect remains valid under inert atmosphere and conventional AlCrFeNiSi LPBF laser-power, scan-speed, layer-thickness, dimensional, and thermal ranges.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis initially describes comparison with 'conventionally fabricated parts,' which ordinarily denotes non-AM fabrication, but the outcome, baseline, and experiment use room-temperature-build-plate LPBF as the comparator.
